title: Plain copy takes the layer you picked, copy merged takes everything
goal: Select a layer, draw a marquee, press copy, and you get the pixels of every layer flattened together rather than the pixels of the layer you had picked. That is the merged copy, and it should be the one that needs a modifier. Plain copy should take the picked layer inside the selection, and copy from all layers should be command shift C, which is where Photoshop puts copy merged.
notes: Reported by the user on 2026-09-07. Confirmed by reading: EditorState.copySelectedLayer (Sources/Photonz/EditorState+Clipboard.swift line 23) begins by checking whether a pixel region is selected and, if so, calls copyRegionFromComposite and returns, with a comment stating the rule deliberately: a pixel region supersedes the layer, command C copies the region not the layer. The region is taken from the COMPOSITE, which is why every layer comes with it. Meanwhile command shift C is already taken by Copy Image (EditorCommands.swift line 130), which copies the whole flattened canvas; that is Photoshop's Copy Merged in spirit and its shortcut, so the two can converge rather than fight: make command shift C mean copy merged, of the selection when there is one and of the whole canvas when there is not, and let plain copy take the picked layer. Keep the existing behaviour where a copied measurement also travels as its spec line. Also worth checking while there: New Layer via Copy (line 304) and the cut path, since both share the same idea of what a selection means.
acceptance: With a layer picked and a marquee drawn, plain copy puts that layer's pixels inside the selection on the clipboard and nothing from the layers around it
Command shift C copies every layer flattened together inside the selection, and says so in the menu
With no marquee drawn, plain copy still copies the picked layer as a whole, exactly as it does now
With nothing picked and a marquee drawn, the audit says what plain copy does and why that is the sensible answer
Both land as a picture other apps can paste, and Photonz's own paste puts them back where they belong
The menu names both plainly, so the difference is readable without trying it
Pasting into another app is checked by hand, not only inside Photonz
Audit written under queue/audits/ with a two layer document, a marquee, and both copies pasted back, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: review before building: copy is the ONLY region op that takes the composite. Fill (fillRegion), erase (deleteRegion) and drag-a-region (beginRegionMove) already target the picked layer via regionTargetID. So the fix is not a new idea, it is copy catching up with the rest of the app.

review: a marquee that misses the picked layer would copy a fully transparent rectangle, which pastes as an invisible layer and looks broken. Decided: copy nothing and beep, the way Photoshop refuses an empty selection.

review: a marquee much bigger than the layer would copy a small drawing floating in a big transparent box. Decided: trim the copy to its own pixels, which is what deleteRegion already does when it slices a layer (bounds derived from content).

review: cut is worse than copy today. With a marquee up, command X copies the flattened region and then deletes the WHOLE layer, and with nothing picked it does nothing at all. Fixing copy without cut would leave copy taking a region and cut taking a layer. In scope.
review: new layer via copy (command J) has the same composite habit. Leaving it alone this run and filing it, since it is a different command with its own audit history.

review: decided NOT to make a marquee that fully contains the layer copy the layer itself (editable text, live model). It is tempting but it makes one key do two different things depending on where the marquee edge falls, and acceptance asks for a picture other apps can paste. Filed as a follow-up thought instead.

shape: routing decided in PhotonzCore (CopyRoute/CopyPlan, tested), isolating one layer in place decided in PhotonzRender (render(_:store:only:), tested), the app layer only carries it to the pasteboard.
release scope: EditorState is shared code, so the change rides a next-scoped flag (next-copy-picks-your-layer), on by default in Next, and Current keeps today's behaviour.

built: CopyRoute + CopyPlan in PhotonzCore (9 tests) decide picked-vs-merged; DocumentRenderer.render(_:store:only:) in PhotonzRender (4 tests) draws one layer alone in place; EditorState+Clipboard carries the result to the pasteboard. Whole suite green at 4449 tests.

menus: File > Copy Image becomes Edit > Copy Merged on the same shift-command-C, directly under Copy, so the pair reads together. Verified in the probe's own menu bar reading and in a real screen capture of the menu.

review after building, on the real app: plain copy of the picked layer's marquee comes back 200x150 at the right spot with no photo in it; copy merged comes back 400x300 with the photo; with nothing picked both agree; with no marquee copy is unchanged (layer payload only) and copy merged is the old whole picture hand-off; a marquee that misses leaves the clipboard empty and beeps; cut slices the picture layer and leaves the shape above it alone.
another process read the clipboard the way a pasting app does and got a 200x150 picture of the copied piece. A hand paste into a named app was not done: the loop is not allowed to drive other apps.
rough, filed rather than fixed: command J still promotes the composite; cutting part of a shape still takes the whole shape; the marquee has no keyboard shortcut. Three tasks filed.
open question for the user, in the audit rather than as a decision card, since it does not block: nothing on screen says which copy you just took.
